To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Gender and age are associated with job pride, and job satisfaction.
(1) gender differences in pride in work vary with age, and that (2) the age graded gender difference is in the opposite sense for pride in work than for satisfaction with work.

(1) women report less pride in work than men in early career, but more pride in work in later career; (2) men report less job satisfaction than women in early career, and more job satisfaction than women later in career; (3) the gender differences in job satisfaction and job pride are not related, and are not due to differences in age, income, education, marital status, or employment status.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how pride in work and job satisfaction vary by gender and age.
the role of pride in the work context.
how gender and age shape job pride, job satisfaction, and wellbeing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
women are less likely than men to report pride in their work in their twenties, but more likely than men to do so from midlife to retirement.
gender and age differences in job pride are more strongly influenced by gender and age differences on the nature of the work done, than by differences in the orientation of workers to the work done.
pride is a more important motivator than satisfaction for women, and that pride is a less important motivator than job satisfaction for men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gender and age differences in job pride are linked to gender differences in orientations towards intrinsic rewards and age differences in orientations towards extrinsic job resources.
job satisfaction is a function of the resources that one has, while job pride is a function of doing.
job pride and job satisfac-tion are distinct constructs that have differential relationships with gender and age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age and gender differences in job satisfaction and job pride are not the same.
pride in work is a useful concept that may provide a more nuanced understanding of the wellbeing of workers in the workplace than does job satisfaction alone.
the gender difference in job pride and the gender difference in satisfaction are not the same.
